title: Coordinate-first briefs with mandatory consumer-check and claim-labelling
hypothesis: Delegated subtask cost is driven by rediscovery and rework, not by verification. Giving implementers the file and line coordinates the coordinator has already verified, and requiring two things in every brief - list every consumer of anything you delete or change, and label each claim as verified by command output, derived from code, or not verified - will reduce tool calls per agent run without increasing rework or missed defects.
primaryMetric: Tool calls per delegated implementation subtask agent run
metricSource: Agent run completion metadata reported to the coordinator for each delegated subtask, recorded manually in the Work OS subtask summary. There is no automatic collector; the coordinator records the number from each completion notification.
guardrailMetrics: Share of implementation subtasks requiring a rework round, measured from Work OS review outcomes
Count of BLOCK or CRITICAL findings raised by independent review per implementation subtask
Count of undisclosed out-of-scope file changes found by the coordinator or reviewer

baseline.source: Measured over the 12 agent runs of this session: 569 total tool calls divided by 12 runs. Component runs ranged from 28 to 94 calls. Mean duration 9.3 minutes per run over 111.5 minutes total. Rework baseline: 2 of 6 completed implementation subtasks required a second round, and one further subtask was returned for rework, giving a rework share of roughly one third. Verification cost was separately measured at 12 seconds for the full lint, build and test gate, so verification is explicitly not the cost driver.

audience: The next three delegated implementation subtasks, expected to be QW-0004-S05, QW-0004-S06 and QW-0004-S07. Independent review agents are excluded, because their job is to rediscover evidence independently and shortening that would defeat the control.
stopRule: Stop immediately and revert to the previous brief style if the rework share rises above the one-third baseline, if any BLOCK or CRITICAL finding is traced to an implementer relying on coordinator-supplied coordinates that turned out to be wrong, or if an undisclosed out-of-scope change occurs in two consecutive subtasks.
decisionRule: Keep if mean tool calls per run fall by at least 15 percent against the 47.4 baseline while rework share and BLOCK or CRITICAL counts do not rise. Iterate if cost falls but a guardrail worsens slightly. Stop if cost does not fall or any guardrail clearly worsens.

reviewTrigger.value: Review after three delegated implementation subtasks have completed under the new brief format

risks: Coordinator-supplied coordinates may be stale or wrong, and an implementer that trusts them without checking could ship a defect. Briefs must still require the implementer to confirm each coordinate before editing.
Tool-call counts are a proxy for cost and can be gamed by batching; the guardrails exist so that a lower count achieved by doing less real work is caught as rework or as a review finding.
The sample of three subtasks is small and the result will be indicative, not conclusive.
notes: Verification was explicitly excluded as a cost-reduction target. Independent review found four defects in this session that lint, build and test did not catch, including registration read paths that silently returned empty, a false sponsored label, a bypassable safety guard and an undisclosed validator change.
